## The finding

`crimes scan src/api/state.ts --format json` surfaces exactly **one** `singular_plural_type_mismatch` finding (`crime_00033`), covering **two** declarations:

> **charge:** "Plural Mismatch" · **severity:** `low` · **confidence:** `0.7` · **lines:** `[24, 27]`
> **summary:** "2 declarations whose plural form disagrees with the annotated type's array shape."
>
> **evidence:**
> - "plural name, singular type: `users: User` @L24"
> - "singular name, array type: `invoice: Invoice[]` @L27"
> - "v1 detector — type aliases and generic types are silently skipped"
>
> **fix_shape:** "make the name agree with the type — `users` for array, `user` for scalar"

That last evidence line is a coverage caveat, not a defect: any mismatch expressed through a type alias (`type Users = User[]`) or a generic (`Array<User>`, `Promise<Invoice[]>`) would not appear here, so "every finding" means every one this detector version can see.

## Declaration 1 — `users: User` @L24

```ts
export const users: User = { id: "u_1", email: "a@b.c" };
```

Evidence verbatim: *"plural name, singular type: `users: User` @L24"*

**The type carries the intended meaning.** The annotation and the initializer agree with each other and outvote the name: `User` is a single-object interface (`id`, `email`), and the initializer is one object literal, not an array. The name is the lone dissenter. So this is option **(a) rename**, not a type change — reshaping to `User[]` would mean rewriting the initializer to `[{ ... }]`, i.e. inventing a collection that no code asked for.

**Complication the finding doesn't mention:** the obvious rename target is occupied. Line 33 already declares `export const user: User = { id: "u_2", email: "x@y.z" }` — one of the detector's negative controls. So `users` → `user` is a name collision in the same module. Rename to a qualifier that says which user this is (`currentUser`, `defaultUser`, `seedUser`), or — if `users` and `user` are duplicates of the same idea — delete one.

## Declaration 2 — `invoice: Invoice[]` @L27

```ts
export const invoice: Invoice[] = [];
```

Evidence verbatim: *"singular name, array type: `invoice: Invoice[]` @L27"*

**The type carries the intended meaning again**, and more decisively than in the first case. The initializer is `[]` — an empty array literal. A type change to satisfy the name (`invoice: Invoice`) is not mechanical: there is no single `Invoice` value to put there, so you'd have to fabricate one or make it nullable. Option **(a) rename to the plural** is the only cheap move.

**Same collision:** `invoices: Invoice[] = []` already exists at line 34. So `invoice` → `invoices` shadows an identical declaration. Either merge the two (they are structurally the same empty array) or qualify the survivor by what it holds — `pendingInvoices`, `draftInvoices`.

## Which side wins, generally

Both declarations resolve the same way: **the type wins, because the initializer independently corroborates it.** When name, type, and value disagree, the value is the tiebreaker — it's the thing the runtime actually observes. Names are also the cheaper side to change: these are module-scope exports, and nothing in the fixture imports them, so renames carry no caller churn. The finding's own `suggested_actions` ranks this the same way — `"rename_or_reshape"`, risk `low`.

## One caveat before you refactor

This file is deliberately incriminating. Line 2 says `// This file is fixture material — do not import it from real code`, and lines 23 and 26 are comments naming the detector that each declaration exists to trip. Lines 29–34 are labelled negative controls, which is exactly why `user` and `invoices` are sitting on the rename targets.

So the honest recommendation for this file in this repo is: **leave it alone.** Applying the renames above would silence `crime_00033` and quietly delete the fixture's coverage of the detector. If you want the finding suppressed rather than fixed, the finding names the intended escape hatch:

> "If the project intentionally diverges, add the name to `detectors.options.singular_plural_type_mismatch.allowedNames`."

The rename proposals above are the right answer for a real `state.ts`. Say the word if you want them applied here anyway — that's a scope call, and it costs the detector its regression fixture.
